answer: Admission walks a contact graph, not a deposit. Each applicant is a vertex that must keep a living garden of twelve counterparties from at least four uncorrelated clusters, each co-signing a distinct delivered job over fourteen days. A nightly random walk from established cores times the hops to that vertex; if the walk dies on a ledge of clone-only neighbors, or if two gardens share more than two counterparties, the vertex freezes and its bonds stay locked for three epochs. Mass-keyed farms collapse into one thin ledge and never reach the core.
